examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
model: from-yml  # yml file
retry: 1

.troupe/troupe.yaml:
model: from-yaml  # yaml file
retry: 2

results.1: exit 4, prints nothing. The two arms' error messages differ only in wording. One arm: `troupe: .troupe: both troupe.yml and troupe.yaml exist`. One arm: `troupe: ./.troupe/troupe.yml: both troupe.yml and troupe.yaml exist`
results.2: exit 4, prints nothing. Each of the four arms words the error differently. One arm: `/theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml: both troupe.yml and /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yaml exist` (no `troupe:` prefix). One arm: `troupe: .troupe/troupe.yml and .troupe/troupe.yaml: both exist; keep only one`. One arm: `troupe: both /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml and /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yaml exist; remove one`. One arm: `troupe: error: ambiguous configuration: both .troupe/troupe.yml and .troupe/troupe.yaml exist`

results.1: exit 4, same error as above. Neither file is changed (retry stays 1 in .yml and 2 in .yaml)
results.2: exit 4, same error as above in all four arms. Neither file is changed

results.1: each gives exit 4 with the same error and no output, in both arms
results.2: each gives exit 4 with the same error and no output, in all four arms

context.in_practice: In practice the two routes behave the same: any config command, even just reading a value, fails with exit 4 and changes nothing. The only difference is the error text. Only two arms on route 2 tell the user what to do next ("keep only one" / "remove one"). The case where neither file exists was not tested.
context.stakes: If a project ends up with both `.troupe/troupe.yml` and `.troupe/troupe.yaml`, the user either gets a clear refusal or has one file silently override the other. In the run, every implementation on both routes refused every config command, including read-only ones, until one of the files is removed.
context.tradeoff: Both routes cost the same: config is unusable until the user deletes one file. Route 1 reached this as a deliberate choice; route 2 reached the same behavior without considering the question, and its error messages vary more from arm to arm.

plan_why: Both .troupe/troupe.yml and .troupe/troupe.yaml exist with different values; shows whether get/show/set/history refuse with exit 4 or silently pick one file (and which one), and whether set rewrites a file. The 'neither' case can't be shown because the files are created before every command and can't be removed.
